findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — a user can receive a notification email (e.g. via a category watch or a mention) without ever having a topic_users row. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, producing a NoMethodError and a 500 for exactly the users most likely to click an unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` or handle the nil case by creating the record.

findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates state via a GET request
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action is exposed via GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately writes to topic_users (setting regular/muted). GET links in emails are followed by mail-client prefetchers, link scanners, and antivirus proxies, so a user's notification state can be changed without any intentional action; it also makes the endpoint CSRF-able via a simple tag for logged-in users. The GET should render a confirmation page that performs the change via POST, as the client-side unsubscribe template suggests was intended.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe client route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
findings.body: The `topicUnsubscribe` route (path `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`) is declared after the `topic` resource, whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with nearPost="unsubscribe" before the new route is ever reached. The unsubscribe page will instead load the normal topic route and attempt to treat "unsubscribe" as a post number. The route needs to be declared before the topic resource or nested so it wins.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but most callers don't provide it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` text now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send. The interpolation should be conditional on the URL being present (or all callers updated and a test added for the missing-arg case).

findings.title: Unsubscribe sets notification_level directly, losing reason/changed-at bookkeeping and MessageBus notification
findings.body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and saves the model directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. That bypasses setting `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and skips the MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish, so any other open browser tabs of the user will keep showing the old notification state for the topic until reload, and analytics/auditing of why the level changed is lost.
